title: What is known about 1RB0RD_1RC1LE_1LD---_1RF0LE_1LD1LE_1RA0RF
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RD_1RC1LE_1LD---_1RF0LE_1LD1LE_1RA0RF.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The head sweeps the whole tape. The background is the pair 10, and the leftward sweep over it is a proved shift rule. Short walls (1, 0, 000, 0000 and phase changes) split it into domains whose lengths fall roughly by halves from the left end to the right end. How the walls move has not been made into a rule. Lean proves no halt in the first 10,000 steps by the kernel alone and in the first 107 with native_decide, and proves the shift rules of the sweeps (lean/Rules.lean); the C simulator finds no halt in the first 109 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (C1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 36,175 cells have been visited and 18,177 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.52). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.242).

claims.title: Shift rules of the sweeps
claims.text: The leftward sweep over the background: L (10)^n D>1 R and L (01)^n E>0 R cross a whole domain, 2 steps a pair, leaving it as it is, for every n and all tapes L, R.

claims.title: Domains shrinking by halves
claims.text: Read at the right end at step 398,057,107 (width 23,283) the domains from the left are about 5205, 1301, 1129, 495, 556, 411, ... pairs long and the right end of the tape is a mix of pieces a few pairs long; at step 1,993,416,764 (width 50,020) the first two are 11,712 and 2932. Seen at every end turn; not proved.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The machine halts on C1, reached as B>0 1 (B reads 0, moves right onto a 1). Inside a domain of 10 the sweeps never do that; whether a wall ever does is open, and the walls have no known rule.

check: python3 holdouts/1RB0RD_1RC1LE_1LD---_1RF0LE_1LD1LE_1RA0RF/py/rules.py | diff - holdouts/1RB0RD_1RC1LE_1LD---_1RF0LE_1LD1LE_1RA0RF/lean/Rules.lean   # the rules file is current

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The tape is the pair 10 repeated, broken by many short walls. Near the left end the stretches between walls are thousands of cells long, toward the right end only a few. The head crosses the stretches by a proved rule; the walls follow no rule anyone has found.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 36,175 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).
Ratio of consecutive domain lengths near the left end, roughly.

sections.heading: Pairs 10 and many walls
html: The background is 10 (read 01 in the other phase). The leftward sweep over it is a proved shift rule (lean/Rules.lean). The right end of the tape at step 398,057,107 (width 23,283), long runs written as powers:

sections.heading: Long domains on the left, short on the right
html: The domains are longest at the left end and shrink toward the right roughly by halves (5205, 1301, 1129, 495, 556, 411, ... above; 11,712 and 2932 first at step 2·109). The right end is a dense, irregular mix of short periodic pieces. A similar picture appears in 1RB1LC_1RC---_1LD1LC_1RE0LC_1RF0RE_1RA0RD of the same batch (a different machine).

sections.heading: One pattern at a wall
html: C1 is the only halting transition, reached as B>0 1. Inside a domain this never happens; a halt would have to come from a wall. That is open.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.52). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.242).
After 109 steps the tape spans 36,175 cells (24,182 left of the start, 2,660 right), with a density of 1s of 0.502.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: A bouncer over the background 10 with many short walls; the domains between walls are longest at the left end and shrink roughly by halves toward the right, where the tape is a dense mix of short periodic pieces. No rule for the walls is known.
